observations.observation: Routing is keyed by a stable provider/model identity and records retry, cooldown, fallback, health and snapshot state.
observations.strength: Catalog and route decisions are explicit and auditable.
observations.weakness: A Python gateway is not proof of Omnia's native provider boundary or credentials handling.
observations.decision: Translate identity, snapshot lineage, stale-model state and typed retry decisions into an Omnia-owned adapter; do not vendor LiteLLM.

observations.observation: Fallback and run lifecycle preserve typed attempt lineage, cancellation and retry predicates rather than hiding failures behind text.
observations.strength: Continuation and cancellation boundaries are explicit.
observations.weakness: The Python adapter does not prove Tauri/Rust or live-provider behavior.
observations.decision: Adopt typed effective-effort and retry outcomes with session/run lineage and bounded recovery; keep native gaps visible.

observations.observation: Ask-user is a typed suspension/resume boundary with bounded options, free text, explicit approval outcomes and run binding.
observations.strength: Stale, duplicate and unknown decisions can be rejected without parsing sentinel text.
observations.weakness: Packaged Windows delivery and live provider execution remain unproven.
observations.decision: Keep the native broker contract typed and add packaged-boundary evidence before changing CHAT-008 to Done.

buildEvidence.limitation: Cycle 6 receipt is preview/renderer evidence only; it does not prove native or live provider behavior.

decisions: Keep catalog identity and snapshot lineage separate from renderer display state.
Resolve requested effort to an explicit effective value with unsupported capability evidence; never silently claim xhigh or ultra support.
Carry provider profile and model identity on the session route so Chat, Browser and IDE can share a stable run context.
Retain CHAT-008 as partial until a packaged Tauri command/UI boundary is exercised; native broker unit tests are insufficient.
